config.title: Rotting Oranges

intro.title: Rotting Oranges
intro.body: In this lesson, you will implement an algorithm to simulate the rotting of oranges in a grid. You'll learn how to use a breadth-first search (BFS) approach to track the spread of rot across adjacent cells. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays for the grid and a queue data structure to manage the BFS process. This exercise will help you practice working with 2D arrays, queues, and iterative lesson-solving in a step-by-step manner.
intro.usecase: The Rotting Oranges algorithm models propagation processes like network contagion in social platforms, where a post going viral spreads to connected users. It's used in infrastructure monitoring dashboards to visualize cascading failures in power grids or server clusters as outages ripple through connected nodes. Game developers apply this pattern for area-of-effect mechanics in strategy games, where environmental effects expand turn-by-turn. This BFS approach helps product teams build features that track how states change through connected systems over time.

objectives: Initialize a grid data structure to represent the orange orchard state
Implement a breadth-first search queue to track spreading rot
Manipulate grid coordinates to check adjacent oranges in four directions
Construct a time counter to track minutes until rot propagation completes
Apply boundary checks to prevent array index errors during neighbor traversal
Configure a fresh orange counter to determine when all oranges become rotten
Integrate all components to return the total minutes or -1 for impossible cases
